title: Define per-model graceful-degradation SLI schema and automated error-budget reclamation
creator: Ava Chen
description: Problem statement: We need a standardized, machine-readable SLI schema that is defined per model+endpoint (not just per route), plus a safe automated policy to reclaim unused error budget for controlled burst capacity and regional failover. Current SLOs are route-centric and do not capture model-specific quality regressions nor allow safe short-term budget reuse for emergency bursts. Scope: 1) SLI schema definition (latency, availability, and quality signals) keyed by model_id + route + mode (streaming vs non-streaming). 2) Error-budget reclamation policy (time-bound, reversible, observable) that allows reclaiming a fraction of unused budget to a shared burst pool. 3) Integration points for multi-region failover (progressive circuit-breakers that honor per-model budgets) and token-aware load-shedding. Out of scope for this ticket: billing model changes and per-customer custom SLO contracts (handled separately).
sli_definitions: latency_p95: fraction of requests where server-side first-token latency <= 300ms for text-completion routes; measured per model_id and model-mode; window=5m; bucketed by region

availability_success_start: percentage of requests that successfully open a stream or return first-byte within 2s for non-streaming. failure reasons include OOM, timeouts, and immediate 5xx. window=1m; measured per model_id+route

quality_regression_score: rolling similarity metric against a stored rolling evalset (bleu/bert-score/embedding-similarity depending on model capability). SLI is defined as median similarity >= baseline - delta where delta is calibrated per model family. window=24h; computed per model_id

tail_latency_p999: measure for protective circuit-breakers. If P999 > threshold for two consecutive 5m windows, trigger progressive shedding for non-critical routes for that model in the affected region
kv_cache_hit_rate: fraction of requests that benefit from prefix/KV cache hits. Used as an adjunct SLI to prioritize cache-warm models for burst reclamation
error_budget_reclamation_policy: reclamation_pool: ephemeral shared pool to which unused error budget may be donated. Max donation cap = 10% of a model's monthly budget by default
reclaim_triggers: triggered at hourly cadence. Only reclaim from models with >72h decay of recent burn and net unused budget > 5%
usage_constraints: reclaimed budget can only be applied for burst capacity in the same region where it was donated unless explicit regional permission exists
timebound_grant: grants are valid for at most 30 minutes then auto-return; must be renewed explicitly by controller to extend

audit_and_rollback: all reclamation actions produce an audit entry. If a donor model's quality_SLI drops below its emergency threshold during a grant window, the grant is revoked and immediate rollback to baseline throttling occurs
visibility: per-model donation/grant metrics must appear in Console -> SLO tab with delta visualization and list of active grants
multi_region_failover_and_circuit_breake: progressive_failover: when a region's per-model availability SLI drops below the regional soft-threshold, route traffic shifts in phases: 10% -> 30% -> 100% to warm-standby region, honoring model variant priority
circuit_breaker_modes: soft, hard. Soft mode reduces concurrency and applies best-effort shedding; hard mode immediately rejects non-essential classes and flips to fallback model variants
breaker_triggers: combines latency_p999 spikes, abrupt kv_cache_hit_rate drops, and availability anomalies. Use weighted scoring to decide soft vs hard mode
coordination: controller writes decision to a region-shared config store and agents in each region subscribe for immediate application. Reconciliation loop at 30s intervals
rollback_criteria: automatic rollback if availability and latency SLIs recover to within 10% of baseline for two consecutive 5-minute windows
load_shedding_and_prioritization: token-aware shedding: for overloaded nodes prefer shedding large-token budget requests first (batch estimated token size > configured threshold)
model-priority matrix: customer-paid tiers > internal infra tests > free-tier. The matrix is configurable per-route and per-model. Grants from error-budget pool respect this priority ordering
graceful-degradation policy: degrade response quality by switching to quantized model variants or reducing max_new_tokens before outright rejection
prefetching and cache warming: during a grant window prioritize models with high historical cache hit rate to maximize throughput gains from reclaimed budget
acceptance_criteria: A machine-readable SLI manifest (YAML/JSON) produced for each model_id and validated by runtime schema; schema stored in config repo
Controller implements reclamation_pool with safe grant/rollback semantics and emits audit logs to the platform audit stream
Console surfaces donation/grant timeline and a per-model projected burn-rate visualization
End-to-end e2e test demonstrating: donate 8% of model A's unused budget -> grant used for a 20min burst in region-x -> donor model maintains quality SLI above emergency threshold after rollback
Runbook updated with recovery steps, TTR targets, and oncall playbook for manual revocation
notes_on_tradeoffs: Trade-off 1: Granular per-model SLIs improve fidelity but increase metric cardinality. Decision: only enable per-model quality SLIs for models with >10k monthly requests by default
Trade-off 2: Reclamation increases short-term risk for donors. Decision: conservative defaults (max 10% donation, 30m grants) and automatic rollback on quality dips
Trade-off 3: Cross-region grants can reduce cold-starts but complicate compliance. Decision: default to region-local grants; cross-region allowed only with explicit opt-in label
implementation_plan: Week 1: finalize SLI schema and config schema; land schema validation in config repo
Week 2: controller prototype for reclamation_pool; unit tests and basic audit logging
Week 3: integrate controller with runtime agent for grant application; implement rollback hooks
Week 4: Console integration + dashboards + e2e test; internal alpha rollout to canary customers
Week 5: collect alpha telemetry, iterate thresholds, and prepare release notes for runtime-1.22
